claim: Simultaneous patch-clamp recordings from multiple neurons offer the highest temporal and subthreshold resolution to analyse local synaptic connectivity.
source: Simultaneous patch-clamp recordings from multiple neurons offer the highest temporal and subthreshold resolution to analyse local synaptic connectivity.
evidence: This is stated as an established fact in the abstract about the capabilities of multipatch recordings.

claim: The multipatch setup can record up to 10 neurons simultaneously.
source: We introduce an in vitro multipatch setup with an automated pipette pressure and cleaning system facilitating recordings of up to 10 neurons simultaneously and sequential patching of additional neurons.
evidence: Directly stated in the abstract as a capability of the introduced system.

claim: The method allowed probing of 150 synaptic connections between 17 neurons in one human cortical slice.
source: This method will facilitate the systematic analysis of microcircuits and allow unprecedented assessment of inter-individual variability.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated in Figure 6A showing recordings from 17 neurons.

claim: The method enabled screening of over 600 connections in tissue from a single patient.
source: We present hardware and software solutions that increase the usability, speed and data throughput of multipatch experiments which allowed probing of 150 synaptic connections between 17 neurons in one human cortical slice and screening of over 600 connections in tissue from a single patient.
evidence: Stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 6F showing 336-694 tested connections per patient.

claim: Feedforward information flow between cortical layers is stereotypical.
source: While it is well established that feedforward information flow between the cortical layers is rather stereotypical (Douglas and Martin, 2004), intralaminar connectivity between different classes of neurons is more complicated and heterogeneous across brain regions (Jiang et al., 2015; Peng et al., 2017; Steiner et al., 2019; Song et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by citation to Douglas and Martin, 2004.

claim: Intralaminar connectivity between different classes of neurons is more complicated and heterogeneous across brain regions.
source: While it is well established that feedforward information flow between the cortical layers is rather stereotypical (Douglas and Martin, 2004), intralaminar connectivity between different classes of neurons is more complicated and heterogeneous across brain regions (Jiang et al., 2015; Peng et al., 2017; Steiner et al., 2019; Song et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations (Jiang et al., 2015; Peng et al., 2017; Steiner et al., 2019; Song et al., 2005).

claim: It remains unclear how observed microcircuit topologies generalize across species.
source: Furthermore, it remains as yet unclear how observed microcircuit topologies generalize across species, or whether inter-individual variability can be observed at the level of neuronal microcircuits.
evidence: Stated as a knowledge gap in the introduction.

claim: Specific cellular and synaptic properties in the human central nervous system have been described.
source: While specific cellular and synaptic properties in the human central nervous system have been described (Kalmbach et al., 2018; Molnár et al., 2016; Szegedi et al., 2016), distinctive features at the microcircuit level have yet to be resolved (Seeman et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Kalmbach et al., 2018; Molnár et al., 2016; Szegedi et al., 2016.

claim: Distinctive features at the microcircuit level in humans have yet to be resolved.
source: While specific cellular and synaptic properties in the human central nervous system have been described (Kalmbach et al., 2018; Molnár et al., 2016; Szegedi et al., 2016), distinctive features at the microcircuit level have yet to be resolved (Seeman et al., 2018).
evidence: Stated as a knowledge gap with citation to Seeman et al., 2018.

claim: Multipatch recordings can reliably detect unitary excitatory and inhibitory synaptic connections due to sub-millisecond and subthreshold resolution.
source: This method can reliably detect unitary excitatory and inhibitory synaptic connections due to its sub-millisecond and subthreshold resolution (Geiger et al., 1997).
evidence: Supported by citation to Geiger et al., 1997.

claim: Multipatch recordings allow for detailed electrophysiological and morphological characterization of recorded neurons.
source: In addition, it allows for detailed electrophysiological and morphological characterization of recorded neurons and can be used across species without the need for genetic modifications in contrast to optogenetics or calcium imaging (Markram et al., 2004).
evidence: Stated as a capability of the method with citation to Markram et al., 2004.

claim: Multipatch recordings can be used across species without the need for genetic modifications.
source: In addition, it allows for detailed electrophysiological and morphological characterization of recorded neurons and can be used across species without the need for genetic modifications in contrast to optogenetics or calcium imaging (Markram et al., 2004).
evidence: Stated as an advantage over optogenetics or calcium imaging with citation to Markram et al., 2004.

claim: Increasing the number of simultaneously recorded neurons can increase the number of probed synaptic connections considerably.
source: Increasing the number of simultaneously recorded neurons can increase the number of probed synaptic connections considerably and generate larger sample sizes from fewer experiments.
evidence: Stated as a logical consequence and demonstrated in Figure 4A showing the scaling relationship.

claim: Various groups have been able to increase the number of simultaneous recordings.
source: Various groups were able to increase the number of simultaneous recordings (Guzman et al., 2016; Jiang et al., 2015; Peng et al., 2017; Perin et al., 2011; Perin and Markram, 2013; Wang et al., 2015), but the operation of multiple manipulators is challenging.
evidence: Supported by multiple citations (Guzman et al., 2016; Jiang et al., 2015; Peng et al., 2017; Perin et al., 2011; Perin and Markram, 2013; Wang et al., 2015).

claim: Several approaches have been reported that automate the patch-clamp process.
source: To address this, several approaches have been reported that automate the patch-clamp process, utilizing automated pressure control systems and algorithms for manipulator movements guided by visual or electrical signals (Kodandaramaiah et al., 2018; Kodandaramaiah et al., 2016; Kodandaramaiah et al., 2012; Perin and Markram, 2013; Wu et al., 2016; Kolb et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations (Kodandaramaiah et al., 2018; Kodandaramaiah et al., 2016; Kodandaramaiah et al., 2012; Perin and Markram, 2013; Wu et al., 2016; Kolb et al., 2019).

claim: Eight or more manipulators on one setup are currently used by only a few labs.
source: However, while simultaneous recordings of up to four neurons are becoming increasingly popular, eight or more manipulators on one setup are currently used by only a few labs, missing out on the opportunity to maximize the potential of this method.
evidence: Stated as an observation about the current state of the field.

claim: Cleaning pipettes for immediate reuse increases the size of recorded neuron clusters.
source: Cleaning pipettes for immediate reuse increases the size of recorded neuron clusters and enables a more complete view of the microcircuit.
evidence: Stated as a benefit of the cleaning approach and demonstrated in Figure 5B,C.

claim: The maximum number of simultaneously recorded neurons is highly limited by spatial constraints imposed by the manipulators.
source: The maximum number of simultaneously recorded neurons is highly limited by the spatial constraints imposed by the manipulators.
evidence: Stated as a limitation of multipatch setups.

claim: Pipette cleaning has been implemented for automated patch-clamp of single neurons in vivo and in vitro.
source: This technique has already been implemented for automated patch-clamp of single neurons in vivo (Kodandaramaiah et al., 2018) and in vitro (Kolb et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to Kodandaramaiah et al., 2018 and Kolb et al., 2019.

claim: The automated pressure and cleaning system can record up to 10 neurons simultaneously.
source: We introduce an in vitro multipatch approach with an automated pipette pressure and cleaning system to record up to 10 neurons simultaneously.
evidence: Stated as a capability of the introduced system.

claim: The approach increases the rate of complete clusters and decreases experimental time.
source: Here, we show that this approach and further optimizations increase the rate of complete clusters, decrease experimental time and enable sequential patching of additional neurons.
evidence: Stated as a result and demonstrated in Figure 4D and Figure 5C.

claim: Probing of up to 600 synaptic connections in human brain slices in one day is possible with two setups.
source: We demonstrate that probing of up to 600 synaptic connections in human brain slices in one day is possible with two setups, allowing analysis of microcircuits at the level of individual patients.
evidence: Stated as a demonstrated capability and shown in Figure 6F.

claim: Ten Sensapex uMp-Micromanipulators were arranged on a setup with a Nikon Eclipse FN1 microscope using a custom-made stage.
source: We arranged 10 Sensapex uMp-Micromanipulators on a setup with a Nikon Eclipse FN1 microscope using a custom-made stage which was fabricated by a commercial metal workshop (Figure 1A–C).
evidence: Stated in the methods and shown in Figure 1A-C.

claim: A setup with 8 Scientifica PatchStar manipulators was successfully established on a custom-made stage with a Scientifica SliceScope microscope.
source: We also successfully established a setup with 8 Scientifica PatchStar manipulators on a custom-made stage with a Scientifica SliceScope microscope (Figure 1D; Peng et al., 2017).
evidence: Stated in the methods with citation to Peng et al., 2017 and shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The custom stages consist of a 10 mm aluminium sheet for stability glued to a 1 mm stainless steel sheet to create a ferromagnetic surface for cable routing using magnets.
source: Our custom stages consist of a 10 mm aluminium sheet for stability glued to a 1 mm stainless steel sheet to create a ferromagnetic surface for cable routing using magnets.
evidence: Stated as a description of the custom stage construction.

claim: A 27° approach angle was found to be optimal for the custom-made recording chamber.
source: We found 27° to be optimal for our custom-made recording chamber, which is positioned on an elevated platform.
evidence: Stated as an optimized parameter and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Five MultiClamp 700B amplifiers were connected to one digitizer enabling simultaneous recording of 10 channels.
source: On the 10-manipulator setup, five MultiClamp 700B amplifiers (Molecular Devices) were connected to one digitizer (Power1401-3A with Signal extension from Cambridge Electronic Design) enabling simultaneous recording of 10 channels within the corresponding commercial software Signal (Table 1).
evidence: Stated as a hardware configuration in the methods.

claim: The automated pressure system can be built within a week with basic electrical equipment and does not require extensive technical skills.
source: It can be built within a week with basic electrical equipment and does not require extensive technical skills.
evidence: Stated as a characteristic of the pressure system construction.

claim: LOW pressure is set at 20 mbar for continuous outflow of pipette solution during the idle state in the bath to prevent clogging of the tip.
source: We set one pressure regulator at 20 mbar (LOW) for continuous outflow of pipette solution during the idle state in the bath to prevent clogging of the tip.
evidence: Stated as a specific pressure setting and its purpose.

claim: HIGH pressure of 70 mbar is applied for moving through the slice to approach the cell.
source: We apply 70 mbar (HIGH) for moving through the slice to approach the cell.
evidence: Stated as a specific pressure setting and its purpose.

claim: A previous study demonstrated that dipping the tip of a patch pipette in Alconox solution and applying a sequence of pressure and suction could clean a pipette for immediate reuse.
source: A recent study has shown that dipping the tip of a patch pipette in a specific detergent solution (Alconox) and applying a sequence of pressure and suction could clean a pipette for immediate reuse (Kolb et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Kolb et al., 2016.

claim: More than 10 successful 'repatches' using the same patch pipette were possible with the cleaning protocol.
source: In this study, more than 10 successful 'repatches' using the same patch pipette were possible while no change in the electrophysiological properties of the cells was observed.
evidence: Stated as a result from the cited study (Kolb et al., 2016).

claim: The entire cleaning process takes approximately 1 minute and can be executed for multiple pipettes at the same time.
source: The entire cleaning process takes approximately 1 minute and can be executed for multiple pipettes at the same time.
evidence: Stated as a characteristic of the cleaning process.

claim: Alconox contains 10–20% sodium linear alkylbenzene sulfonate (LAS), which affects Glycin-, GABAA- and GluR6-mediated currents at concentrations around 0.001%.
source: Alconox contains 10–20% sodium linear alkylbenzene sulfonate (LAS), which affects Glycin-, GABAA- and GluR6-mediated currents at concentrations around 0.001% (Machu et al., 1998).
evidence: Supported by citation to Machu et al., 1998.

claim: No significant amount of LAS could be detected in the pipette solution after the cleaning cycles.
source: Since it has already been shown that no significant amount of LAS could be detected in the pipette solution after the cleaning cycles (Kolb et al., 2016), the remaining potential source of contamination is residual detergent adhering to the outside surface of the pipette tip.
evidence: Supported by citation to Kolb et al., 2016.

claim: 67 rat pyramidal neurons were compared before and after cleaning to test possible effects of pipette cleaning solution on cellular and synaptic properties.
source: We compared the cellular properties (resting membrane potential and input resistance), synaptic properties (spontaneous EPSP frequency and amplitude), action potential kinetics (threshold, amplitude, half-width, depolarisation and repolarisation rate) and recording quality (access resistance) of 67 rat pyramidal neurons before (n = 25), and after cleaning (n = 21 after first cleaning and n = 21 after second cleaning, Figure 3I–L).
evidence: Stated in the methods and shown in Figure 3I-L.

claim: No evidence for a systematic change in cellular or synaptic physiology was found after pipette cleaning in rat neurons.
source: While we observed some variability between different recordings, we found no evidence for a systematic change in cellular or synaptic physiology (p>0.05 in all comparisons using repeated measures ANOVA, Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: Stated as a result of statistical analysis with p-values.

claim: The mean relative difference for all parameters were between 0% and 10% after pipette cleaning in rat neurons.
source: The mean relative difference for all parameters were between 0% and 10%.
evidence: Stated as a quantitative result of the comparison.

claim: On a setup with six manipulators, an average of 5.3 ± 0.7 successful recordings per cluster were obtained with an average of 23 ± 7 tested connections.
source: On a setup with six manipulators, we obtained on average 5.3 ± 0.7 successful recordings per cluster with an average of 23 ± 7 tested connections (mean ± standard deviation, n = 30).
evidence: Stated as a performance result and shown in Figure 4B,C.

claim: The six-manipulator setup achieved an average success rate of 88 ± 12%.
source: This corresponds to an average success rate of 88 ± 12% which is calculated as the ratio of successfully recorded cells to the maximum number of pipettes available per cluster (Figure 4B).
evidence: Stated as a calculated performance metric and shown in Figure 4B,C.

claim: After scaling up to eight pipettes, an average of 6.8 ± 1 cells were recorded with a success rate of 85 ± 13% and a mean of 41 ± 13 tested connections.
source: After scaling up to eight pipettes, we could record from 6.8 ± 1 cells on average (success rate 85 ± 13%) which increased the mean number of tested connections to 41 ± 13 (n = 33).
evidence: Stated as a performance result and shown in Figure 4B,C.

claim: On the setup with 10 pipettes, an average of 7.9 ± 1.1 neurons were recorded with 56 ± 17 tested connections and a success rate of 79 ± 11%.
source: On our setup with 10 pipettes, we recorded on average from 7.9 ± 1.1 neurons with 56 ± 17 tested connections which represents a further drop of the success rate to 79 ± 11% (n = 10).
evidence: Stated as a performance result and shown in Figure 4B,C.

claim: The total experimental time needed before the start of recording increased from 36.6 ± 2.3 min (eight pipettes) to 46.1 ± 4.6 min (10 pipettes).
source: Concurrently, the total experimental time needed before the start of recording the electrophysiological properties of the neurons rose from 36.6 ± 2.3 min (eight pipettes) to 46.1 ± 4.6 min (10 pipettes), mostly due to increasing time needed to approach and patch the cells (16.8 ± 2.7 min vs 25.8 ± 2.2 min, Figure 4D).
evidence: Stated as a measured time difference and shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The clean-to-complete strategy increased the average cluster size on setups with 8 and 10 pipettes to 7.8 ± 0.4 (97% ± 5% success rate) and 9.2 ± 0.6 (92% ± 6% success rate), respectively.
source: This clean-to-complete strategy increased the average cluster size on our setups with 8 and 10 pipettes to 7.8 ± 0.4 (97% ± 5% success rate, n = 16) and 9.2 ± 0.6 (92% ± 6% success rate, n = 9), respectively (Figure 5B).
evidence: Stated as a result of the cleaning strategy and shown in Figure 5B,C.

claim: Using both cleaning strategies during rodent experiments on the eight-pipette setup, the number of tested connections increased from 140 ± 24 to 244 ± 52 on average per animal.
source: Using both strategies during rodent experiments on the eight-pipette setup with two to recorded slices per animal, we could increase the number of tested connections from 140 ± 24 to 244 ± 52 on average per animal (Figure 5D, mean ± standard deviation, n = 6 animals).
evidence: Stated as a result of combining cleaning strategies and shown in Figure 5D,E.

claim: Up to 17 neighboring neurons were recorded in one human slice with two rounds of clean-to-extend.
source: With two rounds of clean-to-extend, we were able to record electrophysiological properties and the synaptic connections of up to 17 neighboring neurons in one human slice (Figure 6A).
evidence: Stated as a result and shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Using two setups simultaneously, recordings from up to 99 neurons were obtained, probing 300 to 700 potential synaptic connections from individual patients within the first 24 hr after slicing.
source: Using two setups simultaneously, we were able to record from up to 99 neurons and thereby probe 300 to 700 potential synaptic connections from individual patients within the first 24 hr after slicing.
evidence: Stated as a result and shown in Figure 6E,F.

claim: Excitatory connectivity between pyramidal cells in human cortical layer 2/3 ranged from 12.9% to 17.7%.
source: We found excitatory connectivity between pyramidal cells in human cortical layer 2/3 ranging from 12.9% to 17.7% which is similar to those reported previously (Boldog et al., 2018; Seeman et al., 2018; Szegedi et al., 2016).
evidence: Stated as a result with citations to previous studies and shown in Figure 6G.

claim: The inter-individual differences in connectivity were not statistically different from each other.
source: The inter-individual differences were not statistically different from each other (Pat. 1 vs 2, p=0.08; Pat. 1 vs 3, p=0.26; Pat. 2 vs 3, p=0.41) while they were statistically equivalent within a range of −5 and 9.5% (Pat. 1 vs 2, 4.9% [0.3% 9.5%], Pat. 1 vs 3, 3.1% [-1.5% 7.7%], Pat. 2 vs 3, −1.8% [−5% 1.5%], proportion difference [90% confidence interval of difference]).
evidence: Stated as a statistical result with p-values and confidence intervals.

claim: The substantial improvement in multipatch experiment yield has the potential to facilitate systematic analysis of complex network properties at the level of individuals in humans and other species.
source: This substantial improvement in multipatch experiment yield has the potential to facilitate systematic analysis of complex network properties at the level of individuals in humans and other species.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion about the implications of the results.

claim: Comparing neuronal microcircuits across different brain regions, species and individuals can reveal common and divergent principles of network computation.
source: Comparing neuronal microcircuits across different brain regions, species and individuals can reveal common and divergent principles of network computation.
evidence: Stated as a motivation for the study in the abstract.

claim: The establishment of multipatch recordings is technically complex.
source: However, its establishment is technically complex and the experimental performance is limited by high failure rates, long experimental times and small sample sizes.
evidence: Stated as a limitation of multipatch recordings in the abstract.

claim: The experimental performance of multipatch recordings is limited by high failure rates, long experimental times and small sample sizes.
source: However, its establishment is technically complex and the experimental performance is limited by high failure rates, long experimental times and small sample sizes.
evidence: Stated as limitations of multipatch recordings in the abstract.

claim: Cortical resections from epilepsy or tumor patients represent a unique opportunity to analyze the human cortical microcircuit.
source: Cortical resections from epilepsy or tumor patients represent a unique opportunity to analyze the human cortical microcircuit.
evidence: Stated as a rationale for using human tissue in the introduction.

claim: Availability of human brain tissue is scarce, making it necessary to pool data across patients at present.
source: Availability of human brain tissue is scarce, making it, at present, necessary to pool data across patients.
evidence: Stated as a current limitation in human brain research.

claim: There is high diversity between patients with respect to different environmental and genetic background, medical history and medication.
source: This is problematic considering the high diversity between patients with respect to different environmental and genetic background, medical history and medication.
evidence: Stated as a concern for pooling data across patients.

claim: Increasing the data yield from individual animals would efficiently promote the ethical principle to replace, reduce and refine animal experiments.
source: Apart from that, in non-human studies, increasing the data yield from individual animals would efficiently promote the ethical principle to replace, reduce and refine animal experiments (Russell et al., 1959).
evidence: Stated as a benefit with citation to Russell et al., 1959.

claim: Multipatch recordings still represent the gold standard method to dissect microcircuits compared to various other approaches.
source: To dissect microcircuits, multiple whole-cell patch-clamp recordings (multipatch) still represent the gold standard method compared to various other approaches (Hochbaum et al., 2014; Packer et al., 2015).
evidence: Stated as an assessment of the method with citations to Hochbaum et al., 2014 and Packer et al., 2015.

claim: Multipatch recordings enable the investigation of connection probabilities, synaptic strength, plasticity and higher order network statistics incorporating distance-dependencies.
source: These conditions enable the investigation of connection probabilities, synaptic strength, plasticity and higher order network statistics incorporating distance-dependencies (Song et al., 2005; Thomson and Lamy, 2007).
evidence: Stated as capabilities of the method with citations to Song et al., 2005 and Thomson and Lamy, 2007.

claim: Multipatch setups increase the complexity and time of experiments, necessitating automation.
source: Multipatch setups increase the complexity and time of experiments, necessitating automation.
evidence: Stated as a rationale for automation in the introduction.

claim: The operation of multiple manipulators is challenging.
source: Various groups were able to increase the number of simultaneous recordings (Guzman et al., 2016; Jiang et al., 2015; Peng et al., 2017; Perin et al., 2011; Perin and Markram, 2013; Wang et al., 2015), but the operation of multiple manipulators is challenging.
evidence: Stated as a challenge in multipatch experiments.

claim: Simultaneous recordings of up to four neurons are becoming increasingly popular.
source: However, while simultaneous recordings of up to four neurons are becoming increasingly popular, eight or more manipulators on one setup are currently used by only a few labs, missing out on the opportunity to maximize the potential of this method.
evidence: Stated as an observation about the current state of the field.

claim: The success of a whole-cell recording depends on mechanical interference, deterioration of recording quality during prolonged experimental time and tissue quality.
source: Furthermore, the success of a whole-cell recording depends on mechanical interference, deterioration of recording quality during prolonged experimental time and tissue quality.
evidence: Stated as factors affecting recording success.

claim: These factors are aggravated when the number of pipettes is increased.
source: These factors are aggravated when the number of pipettes is increased.
evidence: Stated as a consequence of increasing pipette numbers.

claim: Sequential recordings from multiple cells using the same pipette would overcome the limitation on maximum cluster size given by the number of manipulators in use.
source: Sequential recordings from multiple cells using the same pipette would also overcome the limitation on maximum cluster size given by the number of manipulators in use.
evidence: Stated as a benefit of pipette cleaning.

claim: Sequential patching will provide a more complete view of the microcircuit enabling the analysis of more complex network motifs and higher degree distributions.
source: This will provide a more complete view of the microcircuit enabling the analysis of more complex network motifs and higher degree distributions (Perin et al., 2011; Song et al., 2005; Vegué et al., 2017).
evidence: Stated as a benefit with citations to Perin et al., 2011; Song et al., 2005; Vegué et al., 2017.

claim: Expanding a setup from a single or dual patch-clamp configuration to one with more patch pipettes is primarily an issue of spatial arrangement of the micromanipulators.
source: Expanding a setup from a single or dual patch-clamp configuration to one with more patch pipettes is primarily an issue of spatial arrangement of the micromanipulators.
evidence: Stated as a key consideration in the methods.

claim: The upscaling of multipatch setups has been accomplished with manipulator systems from different commercial manufacturers such as Luigs and Neumann and Scientifica.
source: The upscaling of multipatch setups has been accomplished with manipulator systems from different commercial manufacturers such as Luigs and Neumann (Guzman et al., 2016; Jiang et al., 2015; Wang et al., 2015; Winterer et al., 2017) and Scientifica (Cossell et al., 2015; Peng et al., 2017).
evidence: Stated with citations to multiple studies (Guzman et al., 2016; Jiang et al., 2015; Wang et al., 2015; Winterer et al., 2017; Cossell et al., 2015; Peng et al., 2017).

claim: A shallow approach angle increases the range of motion in the x-axis which is important to reach both the centre of the recording well and the outside well containing the cleaning solution.
source: A shallow approach angle increases the range of motion in the x-axis which is important to reach both the centre of the recording well and the outside well containing the cleaning solution.
evidence: Stated as a design consideration.

claim: The angle needs to be sufficiently steep to allow the pipette tip to reach into the slice in the z-axis while avoiding touching the wall of the centre well.
source: However, the angle needs to be sufficiently steep to allow the pipette tip to reach into the slice in the z-axis while avoiding touching the wall of the centre well.
evidence: Stated as a design constraint.

claim: There is currently no commercial hardware solution that incorporates more than eight digital-to-analogue converter (DAC) output channels with the same number of analogue input channels in one device.
source: Since there is currently no commercial hardware solution that incorporates more than eight digital-to-analogue converter (DAC) output channels with the same number of analogue input channels in one device, we needed to increase the number of DAC output channels from 8 to 10 on the 10-manipulator setup.
evidence: Stated as a limitation that required a custom solution.

claim: A previous report has demonstrated an electrically controlled pressure system for a multipatch setup.
source: A previous report has demonstrated an electrically controlled pressure system for a multipatch setup (Perin and Markram, 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Perin and Markram, 2013.

claim: Other groups have implemented automatic pressure devices together with pipette movement algorithms for automated in vivo patch-clamp.
source: Other groups have also implemented automatic pressure devices together with pipette movement algorithms for automated in vivo patch-clamp (Desai et al., 2015; Kodandaramaiah et al., 2016; Kodandaramaiah et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to Desai et al., 2015; Kodandaramaiah et al., 2016; Kodandaramaiah et al., 2012.

claim: The Autopatcher by Kodandaramaiah et al. has been developed for multi-neuron in vivo recordings with four pipettes.
source: The Autopatcher by Kodandaramaiah et al. has also been developed for multi-neuron in vivo recordings with four pipettes (Kodandaramaiah et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Kodandaramaiah et al., 2018.

claim: The automated pressure system is applicable to any other patch-clamp setup.
source: This open-source and affordable pressure system is applicable to any other patch-clamp setup.
evidence: Stated as a characteristic of the pressure system.

claim: The automated pressure system can reduce experimental errors, increase the experimental speed and help the experimenter to concentrate on the other tasks essential for successful operation of a multipatch setup.
source: It can reduce experimental errors, increase the experimental speed and help the experimenter to concentrate on the other tasks essential for successful operation of a multipatch setup.
evidence: Stated as benefits of the pressure system.

claim: With the optimal angle and positioning of the manipulators, all pipettes can access the brain slice and the cleaning solution without mechanical interference.
source: With the optimal angle and positioning of the manipulators (Figure 1B), all pipettes can access the brain slice and the cleaning solution without mechanical interference.
evidence: Stated as a result of the design and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The success rate of establishing good recordings was increased by incorporating the cleaning protocol.
source: We implemented this protocol to our multipatch approach, because it was able to increase the success rate of establishing good recordings.
evidence: Stated as a benefit of the cleaning protocol and demonstrated in Figure 5C.

claim: The cleaning process greatly increases the success rate of obtaining recordings and thus the yield of a single experiment.
source: This greatly increases the success rate of obtaining recordings and thus the yield of a single experiment.
evidence: Stated as a benefit of the cleaning process and demonstrated in Figure 5.

claim: The possibility to repetitively perform patch attempts without manual replacement of the pipettes increases the speed of learning and performance of novel experimentalists.
source: We also believe that the possibility to repetitively perform patch attempts without manual replacement of the pipettes increases the speed of learning and performance of novel experimentalists, thus lowering the barrier to establish multipatch setups.
evidence: Stated as a speculated benefit of the cleaning system.

claim: The prefill approach reduces the time to fill and mount all pipettes to 11–13 min.
source: This approach reduced the time to fill and mount all pipettes to 11–13 min, while the time during prefilling can be used for other preparations (Figure 4C).
evidence: Stated as a measured time and shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The semi-automated algorithm reduces the risk of breaking pipette tips and the time needed to complete pipette positioning to 7–9 min.
source: This semi-automated approach reduces the risk of breaking pipette tips and the time needed to complete pipette positioning to 7–9 min (Figure 4C).
evidence: Stated as a measured time and shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Increasing the number of pipettes lowers the rate of obtaining a full cluster with successful recordings on all pipettes, even for skilled experimenters.
source: However, increasing the number of pipettes lowers the rate of obtaining a full cluster with successful recordings on all pipettes, even for skilled experimenters.
evidence: Stated as an observation and demonstrated in Figure 4B,C.

claim: Success rate of patch-clamp recordings can vary greatly depending on tissue health, species, brain region and cell type.
source: Success rate of patch-clamp recordings can vary greatly depending on tissue health, species, brain region and cell type.
evidence: Stated as a consideration for performance analysis.

claim: Manual replacement of failed pipettes was refrained from due to the risk of losing the other recordings.
source: We refrained from manual replacement of failed pipettes due to the risk of losing the other recordings.
evidence: Stated as an experimental decision.

claim: The time needed to approach and patch the cells increased from 16.8 ± 2.7 min for eight pipettes to 25.8 ± 2.2 min for 10 pipettes.
source: Concurrently, the total experimental time needed before the start of recording the electrophysiological properties of the neurons rose from 36.6 ± 2.3 min (eight pipettes) to 46.1 ± 4.6 min (10 pipettes), mostly due to increasing time needed to approach and patch the cells (16.8 ± 2.7 min vs 25.8 ± 2.2 min, Figure 4D).
evidence: Stated as a measured time difference and shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The upscaling of a conventional multipatch setup will become impractical at a certain point considering the drop in success rate and increased experimental time.
source: Considering this drop in success rate and increased experimental time, the upscaling of a conventional multipatch setup will become impractical at a certain point.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion based on the performance data.

claim: The outflow of high-potassium intracellular solution depolarises the other cells during the patch attempt which would affect ongoing nearby recordings.
source: The outflow of high-potassium intracellular solution depolarises the other cells during the patch attempt which would affect ongoing nearby recordings.
evidence: Stated as a reason for not recording during patch attempts.

claim: The initial assessment of electrophysiological parameters takes up to 5 min after patching all cells.
source: This initial assessment takes up to 5 min.
evidence: Stated as a measured time for the assessment protocol.

claim: The connectivity screening protocol records up to 50 sweeps in 10 to 12.5 min depending on the number of neurons in the cluster.
source: Afterwards, we perform a connectivity screening protocol which records up to 50 sweeps in 10 to 12.5 min depending on the number of neurons in the cluster.
evidence: Stated as a measured time for the connectivity protocol.

claim: This would enable exploration of specific connectivity patterns and a more elaborate degree analysis of specific cells.

claim: This approach can unveil complex connectivity patterns between local neurons exceeding simple pairwise statistics.

claim: This represents a substantial increase in performance and experimental output compared to previous studies on synaptic connectivity, which usually require pooling of data across multiple subjects.
source: In this report, we demonstrate that equipping an in vitro multipatch setup with an automated pipette cleaning system and adding further optimizations increases the experimental yield and generates sufficient data for microcircuit analysis within single patients. This represents a substantial increase in performance and experimental output compared to previous studies on synaptic connectivity, which usually require pooling of data across multiple subjects to achieve statistically significant results (Seeman et al., 2018; Thomson and Lamy, 2007).
evidence: Stated as a conclusion with citations to Seeman et al., 2018 and Thomson and Lamy, 2007.

claim: With 300 to 600 probed connections per patient, variant and invariant parameters can be identified.

claim: Applied to animal studies, this approach can reduce the number of animals needed to reach statistically significant findings.

evidence: Stated as a method to address underestimation with citations to Levy and Reyes, 2012 and Jiang et al., 2016.

claim: Simulations of slicing effects on connection probability have shown a correction factor between 1.3 to 1.7.
source: Anatomical reconstructions can help to assess the extent of axon cutting and refine the optimal slicing angle while simulations of slicing effects on connection probability have shown a correction factor between 1.3 to 1.7 (Levy and Reyes, 2012; Jiang et al., 2016).

evidence: Supported by citation to Seeman et al., 2018.

source: Patch-clamp electrophysiology is a widespread and established method, but operating multiple manipulators still requires skilled researchers with long training.

evidence: Stated as a potential application of the presented solutions.

source: Additionally, semi-automated pipette positioning as well as repetitive pipette cleaning without the need for manual replacement can help novel experimentalists to focus on the crucial steps of cell patching and may reduce the training time.

claim: Manual adjustments during the visually guided approach of the cell and the fine-tuned application of pressure yielded higher success rates (88%/85%/79%) compared to a fully automated system (43% to 51%).
source: We found that manual adjustments during the visually guided approach of the cell and the fine-tuned application of pressure to obtain a whole-cell configuration yielded higher success rates (88%/85 % / 79% on the 6-/8-/10-manipulator setup) compared to a fully automated system with pipette cleaning and machine vision which reported a success rate of 43% to 51% (Wu et al., 2016; Kolb et al., 2019).

claim: The semi-automated pipette positioning approach was faster (53/55 s per pipette) than the fully automated method (103 s using one pipette).

(2016) (103 s using one pipette) while the time needed to manually approach the cell and establish a whole-cell configuration was slightly higher (126/154 s per pipette on 8-/10-manipulator setup vs 120 s).
evidence: Stated as a comparison with citation to Wu et al., 2016.

claim: The time needed to manually approach the cell and establish a whole-cell configuration was slightly higher (126/154 s per pipette) than the fully automated method (120 s).
source: Our semi-automated pipette positioning approach was faster (53/55 s per pipette on 8-/10-manipulator setup) than the fully automated method described in Wu et al. (2016) (103 s using one pipette) while the time needed to manually approach the cell and establish a whole-cell configuration was slightly higher (126/154 s per pipette on 8-/10-manipulator setup vs 120 s).
evidence: Stated as a comparison with citation to Wu et al., 2016.

source: Also, slice exchange and cell selection would still require human presence.

claim: Automated data analysis is an essential step to leverage the increased experimental throughput.
source: By overcoming the presented technical limitations, other aspects of the experimental pipeline become a bottleneck and need to be addressed. Automated data analysis is an essential step to leverage the increased experimental throughput.
evidence: Stated as a necessary next step.

claim: A previous study demonstrated an automatic synapse detection algorithm using a support vector machine classifier that achieved an accuracy of 95%.
source: For connectivity studies, a previous study has demonstrated an automatic synapse detection algorithm using a support vector machine classifier that achieved an accuracy of 95% (Seeman et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Seeman et al., 2018.

claim: All-optical approaches using channelrhodopsins and fluorescent indicators can be used to probe connectivity of a higher number of cells than the multipatch approach.
source: Compared to other methods, the multipatch approach provides superior access to cellular and synaptic properties with a trade-off regarding the size of the sampled network. All-optical approaches using channelrhodopsins to stimulate individual neurons and fluorescent calcium or voltage indicators to measure their responses can be used to probe connectivity of a higher number of cells than the multipatch approach (Emiliani et al., 2015).
evidence: Stated as a comparison with citation to Emiliani et al., 2015.

claim: Simultaneous optical stimulation and recording using calcium indicators have been performed in up to 20 neurons.
source: Simultaneous optical stimulation and recording using calcium indicators have been performed in up to 20 neurons (Packer et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Packer et al., 2015.

claim: Calcium transients cannot resolve single action potentials or subthreshold postsynaptic signals, potentially missing monosynaptic connections.
source: However, calcium transients cannot resolve single action potentials or subthreshold postsynaptic signals, potentially missing monosynaptic connections.
evidence: Stated as a limitation of calcium imaging.

source: Voltage indicators can resolve subthreshold signals with higher temporal resolution than calcium imaging and have been shown to detect monosynaptic connections combined with optical stimulation in organotypical slices (Hochbaum et al., 2014).

source: Stimulation through a high-density multielectrode array or two-photon glutamate uncaging allows mapping of monosynaptic inputs from 10 to 50 presynaptic neurons onto a single patched neuron (Fino and Yuste, 2011; Jäckel et al., 2017), while two-photon optogenetic stimulation can probe connections from up to 200 presynaptic neurons in a single experiment (Izquierdo-Serra et al., 2018).

claim: Two-photon optogenetic stimulation can probe connections from up to 200 presynaptic neurons in a single experiment.

evidence: Supported by citation to Izquierdo-Serra et al., 2018.

claim: These approaches do not resolve electrophysiological and anatomical properties and further connectivity of the presynaptic neurons.
source: These approaches do not resolve electrophysiological and anatomical properties and further connectivity of the presynaptic neurons, but they can be used to complement the multipatch approach.

claim: Multipatch experiments do not need genetically modified cells and can be applied on brain slices from a variety of species.
source: Finally, multipatch experiment do not need genetically modified cells and can be applied on brain slices from a variety of species.
evidence: Stated as an advantage of multipatch recordings.
